definition: Ayotle is a French-Mexican company headquartered in Paris, France, that develops computer vision software.
details: It provides technical services based on motion capture and 3D sensors for interactive applications in the media and entertainment industries. The company was co-founded by José Alonso Ybanez Zepeda and Gisèle Belliot in June 2010. Ayotle is mainly focused on the development and implementation of advanced algorithms for computer vision, from video images in all formats to the use of 3D cameras or depth sensors.

explainer.lead: Ayotle is a French-Mexican company that builds computer vision software for interactive media and entertainment. Its work connects motion capture and 3D sensing with applications that can respond to what cameras and depth sensors observe.

tiers.eli5: Ayotle makes software that helps computers understand what cameras see. A camera or depth sensor can notice someone moving, and an interactive application can then respond, a bit like a game reacting when a player waves.
tiers.practitioner: Ayotle provides computer vision algorithms and technical services for interactive applications. Its inputs include video images in different formats and data from 3D cameras or depth sensors, with motion capture used to connect those observations to media and entertainment systems.
tiers.paperLevel: Ayotle is a computer vision software company whose technical scope spans conventional video, 3D cameras, depth sensors, and motion capture. Its central problem is converting visual or depth observations into information usable by interactive applications.
